channel.title: Hürriyet Daily News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Hürriyet Daily News (hurriyetdailynews.com)

item.title: Turkish people spend 1 hour 40 minutes daily on radio, study shows
item.description: People in Türkiye spend an average of 1 hour and 40 minutes per day listening to radio and music content, according to a new study conducted by Türkiye’s media watchdog, the Radio and Television Supreme Council (RTÜK).

item.title: Temu resumes sales in Türkiye under new import structure
item.description: Chinese e-commerce giant Temu has restarted operations in Türkiye after briefly halting cross-border shipments earlier this month.

item.title: Turkish parliament enacts traffic law reform with higher fines
item.description: Turkish authorities have passed a sweeping overhaul of traffic laws, sharply increasing fines and introducing tougher penalties aimed at reducing road fatalities and dangerous driving.

item.title: Turkish scientist elected to United Nations' AI panel
item.description: Professor Melahat Bilge Demirköz was elected to the Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, the Turkish Foreign Ministry has announced.

item.title: 16 detained over money laundering claims tied to OnlyFans
item.description: Turkish authorities have detained 16 people in a probe into alleged money laundering linked to paid adult content shared online, seizing assets valued at around 300 million Turkish Liras ($6.9 million), prosecutors said on Feb. 13.

item.title: Anti-terror panel to propose transitional law for 'social integration'
item.description: Local reports said on Feb. 13 that a parliamentary commission overseeing the government’s "terror-free Türkiye" initiative will propose a transitional law aimed at reintegrating disarmed PKK members into society, according to a draft final report circulated to political parties.

item.title: Activist group Palestine Action wins legal challenge against UK ban
item.description: England's high court on Feb. 13 upheld a challenge to a U.K. government ban on activist group Palestine Action, saying it had interfered with the right to freedom of speech.

item.title: US completes transfer of ISIL detainees from Syria to Iraq: CENTCOM
item.description: The United States Central Command said on Friday it had completed the transfer of detained ISIL group suspects held in Syria to Iraq.

item.title: Int’l climate cooperation ‘antidote to chaos,’ say top UN official at Istanbul talks
item.description: Climate action can act as a stabilizing force in an increasingly volatile world, the U.N.’s top climate official said on Feb. 11, as Istanbul hosted the first strategic planning meeting ahead of the COP31 summit, which Türkiye will host in the Mediterranean city of Antalya.

item.title: Erdoğan: Universities must adapt as Türkiye’s influence grows
item.description: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan has called on Turkish universities to modernize and strengthen their research capacities, saying young people are key to advancing his government’s "Century of Türkiye" vision.
